name: MiDAS Foods International - USA
old_description: Midas Food International’s award-winning dry blends and food development expertise have revolutionized commercial kitchens for over 40 years. Discover why we’re a trusted partner of food manufacturers and restaurant chains nationwide.
about:
MiDAS Foods International operates from its main campus in Oak Park, Michigan, with a second facility in Birmingham, Alabama. The company has been developing dry blends and food solutions for over 40 years. Partners Richard Elias and Gary Freeman lead the business alongside a team of culinary and R&D executives.

The company engineers shelf-stable dry blends — including sauces, gravies, glazes, seasonings, soup mixes, cheese sauces, batter mixes, and dessert bases — that replicate or exceed scratch-made quality. Its combined U.S. R&D and manufacturing footprint exceeds 150,000 square feet, and an affiliate plant in Kashipur, India (Dry Blend Foods) serves more than 20 countries. The culinary team handles custom formulation, clean-label and plant-based ingredient systems, and manufacturing optimization.

MiDAS serves food processors, manufacturers, and casual-dining restaurant chains across the United States. Customers use its blends to replace ready-to-use sauces that are costly to ship and store, reducing SKU count, batching errors, and waste. Regional product lines cover North/Midwest and South/Southeast flavor profiles, from Michigan baked bean seasoning to Nashville hot sauce and Cajun étouffée mixes.

The company emphasizes sustainability: dry blends cut shipping weight, eliminate refrigeration, and lower energy use by three to six times compared with prepared sauces. MiDAS was built to give manufacturers and restaurants a single-source ingredient that delivers consistent flavor, faster prep, and lower total cost.

about:
Michigan Fiber Optic LLC operates from Holton, Michigan, serving businesses, communities, and homeowners across the state. The company's team brings three decades of experience in fiber optic installation, splicing, and network design, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed.

The firm provides end-to-end fiber optic services, including design, cable placement, installation, splicing, termination, testing, and turn-up. Its technicians handle all fiber types—single mode, multimode, ribbon, and tube—in both inside and outside plant environments. The company also offers structured cabling solutions such as Cat5, Cat6, and Wi-Fi system deployment, positioning itself as a single-source provider for fiber projects of any scale.

Customers range from residential homeowners and local businesses to municipal networks and community broadband initiatives. Michigan Fiber Optic responds to emergency repair requests 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, restoring service after cable cuts or outages. Its OTDR testing capability pinpoints faults ranging from minor bends to complete breaks, enabling targeted repairs.

The company emphasizes its readiness—crews are fully trucked and tooled for immediate deployment—and its comprehensive project management from initial design through final turn-up. This turnkey approach, combined with deep field experience, is presented as its core differentiator in the Michigan market.

about:
Micro Metals, Inc. was founded in 1972 by Kenny Driscoll in Colorado Springs, Colorado, at an elevation of 6,272 feet. The family‑owned and operated company began as a precision sheet‑metal fabrication shop and has remained a single‑source manufacturer of custom metal products for over five decades.

Today the firm operates a 141,000‑square‑foot facility with a secured 208,000‑square‑foot outside storage yard. Its highly automated processes include three laser‑cutting systems, waterjet cutting, robotic and manual press brakes, robotic and manual welding, CNC machining (VMC, HMC, VTC), CNC punching, coil punching, rollforming, blanking, assembly, engineering support, and an in‑house powder‑ and liquid‑coating line that is CARC‑certified. The workforce is notable for its tenure: machinists average 15 years on the shop floor, and the engineering department includes several military veterans.

Micro Metals serves customers in telecommunications, U.S. military, energy, climate‑control, construction, and secure‑storage industries, shipping to local, national, and international clients from its central Rocky Mountain location.

The company emphasizes its “one‑stop” model—quoting, designing, manufacturing, assembling, and shipping under one roof—to control lead times and supply‑chain risk. A culture of continuous improvement, family values, and a commitment to Made‑in‑USA production underpin its reputation for speed, trust, and cost‑efficient manufacturing. Philanthropic efforts have also placed Micro Metals parts in humanitarian building projects on four continents.

name: Micro-Precision Technologies, Inc.
old_description: MPT is MIL-PRF-38534 Class H qualified since 1998, QML-38534 listed, certified by DSCC (Defense Supply Center, Columbus, OH). MPT is AS9100D ISO 9001:2015, and ITAR registered.
about:
Micro-Precision Technologies, Inc. was founded in 1998 in Salem, New Hampshire. The company operates as a privately held business specializing in high-reliability electronic packaging.

The company focuses on thick film hybrid circuits screened onto ceramic substrates such as alumina, aluminum nitride, and beryllium oxide. Its capabilities include hybrid assembly with manual and automated surface-mount technology, wire bonding (ball and wedge), die attach, and semiconductor repackaging. Work is performed in a Class 10,000 cleanroom, and the firm also offers FR-4 to ceramic conversion services for improved thermal management.

Micro-Precision serves industrial, military, and medical markets, supplying components for harsh environments including extreme heat, high vibration, downhole mining, deep-sea wells, and space applications. Customers range from original equipment manufacturers to defense primes requiring MIL-PRF-38534 Class H qualified parts.

The company differentiates itself through its long-standing MIL-PRF-38534 Class H qualification (since 1998), QML-38534 listing, and DSCC certification, combined with AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015 quality systems and ITAR registration. Its ceramic substrates provide inherent thermal management advantages over traditional FR-4 boards.

The business distributes replacement body panels, bumpers, mirrors, and related components for a broad range of passenger cars and commercial trucks. name: Microlink Devices Inc
old_description: MicroLink Devices designs and manufactures solar cells and solar sheets for a variety of applications, including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), spacecraft, and terrestrial collectors.These high-efficiency, single- and multi-junction GaAs-based solar cells are manufactured using MicroLink’s...
about:
MicroLink Devices was founded in 2000 in Niles, Illinois, a northern suburb of Chicago. The company operates a 30,000-square-foot facility that houses a clean room, device fabrication and test laboratories, and a full suite of metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) tools for high-volume epitaxial growth. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company designs and manufactures III-V epitaxial materials for wireless communications, including cellular phones, and produces high-efficiency single- and multi-junction gallium arsenide (GaAs) solar cells and sheets for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), spacecraft, and terrestrial collectors. Its proprietary epitaxial lift-off (ELO) process separates the solar cell structure from the growth substrate, yielding lightweight, flexible cells while allowing the substrate to be reused multiple times. MicroLink owns all equipment needed for growth, fabrication, and testing of epitaxial materials and solar devices.

MicroLink serves the aerospace, defense, and renewable energy sectors. Since 2003 it has been a prime federal contractor on more than thirty programs developing solar cells, transistors, and lasers. Its customer base includes government agencies and commercial firms seeking custom epitaxial materials, solar sheets for UAVs and satellites, and contract research and development support.

The company emphasizes quality and technical depth: it is ISO 9001 certified, employs staff recognized as experts in GaAs- and InP-based device growth and processing, and supports customers through both development and production phases to improve yield and performance. The ELO technology, developed through its federal R&D programs, is cited as a key differentiator that reduces cost and enables flexible, high-specific-power solar solutions.

name: Micross Components - TX, LLC
old_description: With over 40 years of in-depth expertise, Micross CMS provides an unparalleled array of hi-rel microelectronic product, packaging, test & qualification capabilities servicing the space, defense, aerospace, medical, communications, & other hi-rel markets. From pioneering RHSD in 1984, Micross remains the leader as the one source solution for component services. Turnkey & SMI available, S20.20 Certified.
about:
Micross Components - TX, LLC operates from Round Rock, Texas. The company's expertise dates to 1984 when it pioneered robotic hot solder dip (RHSD) for high-reliability microelectronics. It functions as an independent subsidiary within the Micross group, alongside Integra Technologies and SemiDice.

The facility provides a broad suite of component modification and qualification services. Core processes include BGA reballing, robotic hot solder dip, lead attach, column grid array (CGA) attachment, and lead trim/form and reconditioning. Additional capabilities span printed circuit board assembly, rework, and repair, as well as component harvesting from existing assemblies. Support services encompass tape-and-reel packaging, 3D scanning, bake-and-package cycles, marking, labeling, and kitting. The company also performs component qualification testing such as fine and gross leak detection, acoustic microscopy, X-ray inspection, and X-ray fluorescence analysis.

Customers come from space, defense, aerospace, medical, and communications sectors, along with other high-reliability markets. The company positions itself as a single-source provider for component-level services, offering turnkey programs and supplier-managed inventory (SMI) options.

The business was built on the premise of enabling the use of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) components in high-reliability applications through modification, testing, and counterfeit mitigation.
